references.text: The original instruction from God to Moses to make the cherubim on the mercy seat, with one cherub at each end, as Bezalel carries out in Exodus 37:8.
The description of the mercy seat (kapporet) as the part where the cherubim were to be placed.
The immediately preceding verse describing that the cherubim were made of hammered work.
The continuation describing the position of the cherubim with outstretched wings covering the mercy seat.
Solomon made two large cherubim of olive wood for the inner room of the temple, expanding on the symbolism from the tabernacle's cherubim.
The ark of the covenant with the cherubim was placed in Solomon's temple, under the wings of the large cherubim.
Hebrews refers to the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat and points back to the construction of the tabernacle.
This is the direct fulfillment of God's instruction in 25:19 to make the cherubim as one with the atonement cover.
The first part of the same instruction that the source verse fulfills; together they give a complete picture of the structure of the atonement cover.
